decisions: NULL IS NOT 0.00 AND THAT IS THE WHOLE MODEL. A price SET - including 0 - means the station OFFERS that water type; NULL means it does not. 0 is a real price (company-owned stations fill free), so it can never be collapsed into 'no price'. Any ?? 0, Number(x) || 0 or truthiness check reintroduces the bug the schema was shaped to prevent.

THE FREEZE IS AGAINST PRICE EDITS, NOT AGAINST CHANGING WHICH STATION FILLED. Editing a station's price later must not reprice history, but a trip that actually filled elsewhere is a wrong record, not a protected one - so a station change RE-TAKES the cost. A DELIVERED trip is never re-snapshotted; its cost has been reported and moving it would restate a closed period.

costPatch: null (do not touch) and { filling_cost_sar: null } (moved, new station does not price this type) are DIFFERENT CLAIMS and the type keeps them apart. Writing null over a delivered trip's cost would wipe a reported figure.

THE GATE IS ONE RULE READ FROM TWO DIRECTIONS - selectableWaterTypes narrows the TYPE for a fixed station (trip creation), stationBlockedForType narrows the STATION for a fixed type (station change). Only the first existed at capture time, and KI-026-0062 proved it: a potable in-transit trip moved to Umm Al Hamam, which does not fill potable at all. Both live in lib/station-pricing.ts and the actions call ONE pure decideStationChange.

0114 IS A TRIGGER, NOT A CONSTRAINT, because 13 potable trips at Umm Al Hamam predate per-type pricing and are legitimately grandfathered. A CHECK is retroactive and NOT VALID only defers it - a later VALIDATE, or a pg_restore which re-checks everything, would reject the dump. A BEFORE trigger inspects only the NEW row. It applies at EVERY stage including delivered: grandfathering means the existing rows stay, not that more may be made.

TWO triggers, not one: OLD cannot be referenced in an INSERT trigger's WHEN clause, so a single INSERT OR UPDATE trigger would bury the IS DISTINCT FROM test in the body and every unrelated update would enter the function to be told to leave.

pg_trigger_depth() > 1 on UPDATE, because trips_water_station_fkey is ON UPDATE CASCADE - renaming a station KEY rewrites water_station on every trip pointing at it, which looks exactly like a station change and would re-validate the grandfathered rows and refuse a legitimate admin rename. Same technique as 0096's 30-day lock.

SECURITY DEFINER on the trigger function because the failure mode matters: if water_stations RLS is ever narrowed, an INVOKER lookup returns no row, 'not found' allows, and the guard FAILS OPEN silently exactly when someone tightened security. Enforcement must fail closed. No revoke footer - Postgres refuses to invoke a trigger function directly and EXECUTE is checked at CREATE TRIGGER time.
The trigger WRITES NOTHING. filling_cost_sar stays the app's job because the freeze rule lives there; splitting the money rule across SQL and TypeScript is how the gate came apart the first time.

filling_uncosted_trips IS HISTORICAL-ONLY since 0114 - new trips can no longer be uncosted, so the count is fixed at 13 (June-July). A NEW uncosted trip appearing means the guard was dropped, not that the data changed. The count still travels wherever the money is shown, because sum() skips NULLs and those 13 make the historical total short by an unknown amount.

create or replace view can only APPEND (0112 failed with 42P16 on a mid-list insert) and could NOT be dropped, because v_pnl_by_period depends on v_pnl_monthly and 0112 does not recreate it. 0113 follows the same append-only discipline even though nothing depends on it, because 'nothing depends on it today' is a fact with a shelf life. Every view restates security_invoker + revoke anon + grant authenticated after the create - create or replace does not preserve reloptions.

DO NOT SEED A COLUMN WHOSE NULL CARRIES MEANING. A seed migration was drafted and deleted before it ran: it would have turned Umm Al Hamam's deliberate 'no potable' into 'potable at 0', undoing a real business decision under the guise of a backfill.

NEVER RE-DERIVE A BUCKET LIST AT A CALL SITE. The Cost Mix doughnut rendered four hardcoded slices while operating_cost_sar had included filling since 0112 - short by 210 / 1,285 / 4,390 in Jun/Jul/Aug, unnoticed for three months. The direct-cost line needed no change: it reads v_daily_operations.direct_cost_sar as-is.

AN EXPORTED 'use server' FUNCTION IS A LIVE ENDPOINT whether or not a component calls it - 'unused' is not 'unreachable'. updateTrip had no callers and wrote water_station/water_type with neither the gate nor the re-snapshot, so a station change through it would have stranded a frozen cost - a failure 0114 deliberately does NOT catch, because the trigger writes no money.

ONE COLOUR PER COST BUCKET, in lib/cost-colors.ts. Reports and the Dashboard each hardcoded their own hexes and Payroll/Outsourced were SWAPPED between them - worse than two arbitrary palettes, because it looks consistent while meaning opposite things. A leaf module, since the two libs are siblings and neither is the other's parent.

noUnusedLocals + noUnusedParameters are ON as of 6506f2e. A parameter genuinely required by a signature, interface or callback shape gets an _ prefix; it is never deleted, because that changes the shape the caller depends on.

context_notes: READ CLAUDE.md SECTION 7 FIRST - it is the durable record and this file is only a pointer to it; the Water Station Cost entry (migrations 0110-0114) sits just before the deferred tail. Working tree clean, 0 ahead / 0 behind origin/main at 180a27e. Highest migration on disk is 0114. FIVE THINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD. (1) THE FEATURE'S OWN TRAPS ARE IN THE DECISIONS ABOVE - NULL-is-not-zero, the freeze semantics, and why 0114 is a trigger rather than a constraint. Do not re-litigate the grandfathering: 13 Umm Al Hamam potable trips are real history and a constraint of any kind would reject them on the next pg_restore. (2) TWO STANDING TEST SUITES NOW EXIST that need no diagnostic route and no auth bypass - tests/trip-station-gate.spec.ts (8) and tests/cost-colors.spec.ts (3). They drive pure functions, so unlike every earlier suite they do not rot at teardown. The gate spec states its own limit up front: with no Supabase session a server action cannot be exercised end to end, because RLS returns zero stations and the gate then fails to fire FOR THE WRONG REASON while the test still goes green - so it drives decideStationChange, which is the whole decision. The DB half ran against real rows through the MCP and was reverted; trip fingerprint b8e4cdb and the P&L were byte-identical afterwards. (3) NEVER DELETE .next UNDER A RUNNING DEV SERVER. An entire page rendering unstyled was misdiagnosed as a UI regression; the cause was rm -rf .next while the dev server was attached - HTML 200 with every /_next/static/* 404 and .next/BUILD_ID present where dev output belonged. To verify a production build without stopping the server, point distDir elsewhere - and note that next build REWRITES tsconfig.json (reformats it and injects the dist path into include), so revert it afterwards. (4) A GATE HAS TWO HALVES AND THE FRIENDLY ONE STILL MATTERS. The app layer runs first because it refuses before the round trip and can disable the option in the picker; the trigger covers psql, an importer, and a server action nobody has written yet. Both raise the SAME sentence, so a user reads one thing whichever caught it - and the Move-trip modal now shows it instead of a generic retry line. (5) FIGURES AS OF THIS SNAPSHOT, for anything that reconciles later: filling is 210.00 / 1,285.00 / 4,390.00 for Jun / Jul / Aug with 10 / 3 / 0 uncosted; August direct cost is 26,100.42 of which 4,390.00 is filling; the Cost Mix five slices foot to operating_cost_sar with a 0.00 gap in every month.
